guide.summary: OpenProject documents user OAuth through the authorization code flow, with calls made on behalf of the connected person. The api_v3 scope is the broad standard API boundary, so the app must restrict itself to read-only work package calls.
guide.recommendation: OpenProject documents user OAuth through the authorization code flow, with calls made on behalf of the connected person. The api_v3 scope is the broad standard API boundary, so the app must restrict itself to read-only work package calls.

findings.title: Authorization code flow acts on behalf of the connected user
findings.detail: The OAuth application is registered in the instance administration and the authorization code flow returns a bearer token used to make API calls on behalf of the current user. Client ID, client secret and redirect configuration are needed before the first test.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer connects their own OpenProject instance with developer-owned OAuth.

evidence.quote: With the token that you obtained above you can now make API calls to the OpenProject instance on behalf of the current user.
Authorization code flow example

findings.title: api_v3 scope for the standard OpenProject API
findings.detail: api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope and is assumed when no scope is checked. It is broad enough to cover the work packages collection endpoint, but the app must only call read operations and never call create, update or delete endpoints.
findings.appliesWhen: Read-only work package listing through the standard API on the customer instance.

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.

findings.title: Connected person must already be able to view work packages
findings.detail: The read result is limited to work packages the connected person can view in the instance. Confirming representative account access to view work packages is a user prerequisite, and it does not require an additional OAuth scope.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer tests with an account that has view work packages access.

evidence.quote: View work packages – Allows users to view work packages.
Required permission: view work packages (globally or in any project)

steps.title: Register the OpenProject OAuth application on the customer instance
steps.detail: In the customer's OpenProject instance, an administrator opens Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications and clicks the green + OAuth application button. Enter the application name, set the redirect URL provided by the developer's client app, select scope api_v3, mark the application Confidential for the server-side client, and press Create. Record the Client ID and Client secret. The app must only call read operations on work packages.
steps.doneWhen: The OAuth application exists in the instance and its Client ID and Client secret have been recorded by the developer for use in the token exchange.

steps.title: Open the authorization URL and approve read-only API access
steps.detail: Build the authorization request on the customer's instance using the documented endpoint and parameters: response_type=code, the client_id, the redirect_uri, scope=api_v3 and prompt=consent. The connected person signs in and approves access. The browser is redirected to the callback URL with a code parameter. Confirm the code appears in the redirect URL before continuing.
steps.doneWhen: The browser lands on the redirect URL and the URL contains a code query parameter.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.

In this example we skip that server side implementation and just copy the value of the code parameter from the URL that you see in your browser.

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
CLIENT_ID: from the registered OAuth application
REDIRECT_URI: the developer's callback URL configured in the application

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Send a POST to the documented token endpoint with the form fields grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, code and redirect_uri. The response contains access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in and refresh_token. The token is used only for the read calls below.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains an access_token with token_type Bearer and scope api_v3.

evidence.quote: $ curl --request POST \
--data 'redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>' The response will look like this:
The response contains the bearer token (“access_token”) and a refresh token that you will need when working with the API. Please copy the tokens for reference.

fields: AUTHORIZATION_CODE: the code value from the callback URL in the previous step
CLIENT_SECRET: from the registered OAuth application
Keep access_token and refresh_token server-side; do not expose them to the browser
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Read the first page of accessible work package titles
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v3/work_packages with a bearer token and an empty filters array so no default filter is applied. Each element in _embedded.elements holds the title in its subject property. The response _links.nextByOffset or _links.nextByCursor provides the next page when present.
steps.doneWhen: The response is HTTP 200 and returns _embedded.elements with subject values for work packages the connected person can view. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: get /api/v3/work_packages Returns a collection of work packages.
Collections may be paginated, this means that a single response from the server will not contain all elements of the collection, but only a subset. In this case the client
optional query JSON specifying filter conditions. Accepts the same format as returned by the queries endpoint. If no filter is to be applied, the client should send an empty array

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: from the token exchange response access_token
Subject is the work package title; pageSize and offset are documented collection parameters
filters=[] requests all visible work packages instead of the default filter
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Follow the next page link until the collection ends
steps.detail: Repeat the list request using the next link returned in the previous response. For offset pagination, follow _links.nextByOffset; for cursor pagination, follow _links.nextByCursor. Resolve any relative href against the same HTTPS instance host. Stop when the response has no next link or when the returned count is zero. Only read calls are made; no work package is created, updated or deleted. Continue to call the documented next link from each response until the collection ends. This is a continuation of the first work package read; it does not add discovery or enumeration beyond the collection.
steps.doneWhen: The next link is absent in the final response, and every page returned subject values for work packages the connected person can view. A response returns no nextByOffset or nextByCursor link. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

nextByCursor Link to retrieve the elements following the current page (cursor based) when cursor based available

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register the OpenProject OAuth application on the customer instance
In the customer's OpenProject instance, an administrator opens Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications and clicks the green + OAuth application button. Enter the application name, set the redirect URL provided by the developer's client app, select scope api_v3, mark the application Confidential for the server-side client, and press Create. Record the Client ID and Client secret. The app must only call read operations on work packages.
Fields: Instance base URL: user-provided HTTPS origin of the customer's OpenProject instance, Client ID and Client secret: copied from the created OAuth application, Redirect URL: the developer's callback URL, configured identically in the app
